1.why: Sans-serif type with clear headings, comfortable line spacing and high contrast is used throughout, though the Logs panel uses small dense monospace text.

2.why: No italics or all-caps are used and body copy is limited to one or two short sentences per screen, but the Logs panel presents dense unbroken monospace blocks.

3.why: The single-column card layout with full-width buttons would likely reflow acceptably, but only desktop-width screenshots are shown and the recovery-code two-column grid and long secret string risk cramping on a phone.

4.why: Each screen has a one- or two-sentence plain-language instruction such as 'Enter the six-digit identity code' and 'Each recovery code works once.'

5.why: Placeholders show expected formats (marcus@example.com, 15551234567, '6 digits', ABCD-1234-EF56-7890), though the identity verification and authenticator verification fields on steps 2 and 7 are empty with no example.

6.why: Progression only ever requires reading a short heading plus one or two sentences; no long text blocks gate any action, although users must scan the Logs panel to find simulated codes.

7.why: No copy button or copy affordance appears anywhere; the authenticator secret, recovery codes and log values must all be read and retyped by hand.

8.why: No QR code is displayed — step 4 offers only a plain text 'Provisioning information' string and explicitly says manual entry is available instead of scanning.

9.why: Fields have visible labels which may help heuristics, but there is no evidence of autocomplete attributes, no password field, and the one-time-code inputs give no sign of autofill/password-manager support.

10.why: Each screen has a prominent heading and a primary blue button, but there is no step indicator or progress marker, and on steps 7–10 several equally sized buttons compete above the actual input.

11.why: Step 4 asks for the manual secret and the authenticator code at once, step 11 presents two optional code fields plus a challenge button, and the MFA settings screen exposes four actions simultaneously.

12.why: Confirmations such as 'Authenticator verification succeeded', 'Recovery code accepted and permanently consumed' and 'Authenticator MFA is enabled' are shown, but they do not state what comes next.

13.why: Users can retry entries, 'Start over', and regenerate recovery codes, but there is no reveal/hide toggle and codes are explicitly 'displayed once' and cannot be re-requested without invalidating the old set.

14.why: The error on steps 17–18 reads only 'The request could not be completed.', which states neither the specific problem nor how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown timers or session-expiry warnings are visible in any screenshot, but the TOTP design implies time-limited codes and nothing explicitly grants extra time.
